content.title: About
content.content: Italian Ice is a refreshing frozen dessert made from fruit juice, sugar and water. It has a light, slightly granular texture and a vivid fruit flavor. The product contains no dairy ingredients and is suitable for vegans.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Italian Ice originated in Italy in the 19th century as a way to preserve aromatic fruit juices during summer heat.
In the United States it is often called “snow cone,” but unlike snow cones, Italian Ice is made from a frozen fruit mixture rather than shaved ice.
The most popular flavor is lemon, though strawberry, mango, watermelon and mint are also common.
In some regions Italian Ice is served with a splash of alcohol, turning it into a light cocktail.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Italian Ice contains virtually no fat, making it a suitable dessert for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: The fruit juices used provide a good source of vitamin C, which supports the immune system.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Its high water content helps maintain fluid balance, especially on hot days.

items.title: Low‑calorie treat
items.content: A typical serving (≈150 ml) contains about 70–120 kcal, depending on the amount of added sugar.

items.title: Dairy‑free
items.content: Suitable for people with lactose intolerance and for vegans.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High amounts of added sugar can raise blood glucose levels and contribute to tooth decay.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to specific fruits used in Italian Ice.

items.title: Cold sensitivity
items.content: People with sensitive teeth may experience discomfort when consuming this cold dessert.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Italian Ice in cups or cones; you can garnish with fresh berries, mint leaves, or a drizzle of fruit puree. For a richer flavor, let it sit at room temperature for a few minutes before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep Italian Ice in the freezer at –18 °C in an airtight container. Over time ice crystals may form; let the dessert sit for 5–10 minutes at room temperature before serving.
